summary: The study describes the controlled growth of titanium oxide thin films using sequential surface chemical reactions with tetrachlorotitanium (TiCl4) and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) as precursors. The process was investigated using variable-angle spectroscopic ellipsometry, and the growth rates were found to be constant at approximately 0.065 nm per cycle within the temperature range of 340–490 °C. The films exhibited a constant index of refraction of 2.6 and were characterized by AFM and XRD, showing polycrystalline anatase structure.
evidence: Growth rates were almost constant at approximately 0.065 nm cycle-1 ( = 0.65 nm mini) for substrate temperatures from 340 “C to 490 “C. Indices of refraction were also constant at 2.6 in almost the same temperature range.
